tip.en: some in +, any in – and ?: I’d like some water. Have you got any tea?
tip.ru: some в +, any в – и ?: I’d like some water. Have you got any tea?

items.why: In a café “a coffee” means one cup.
any in questions and negatives; some in positive sentences.
I’d like = I would like — a polite request. I like = in general.

lines: “Would you like to see the [menu|menus|a menu]?” — “Thank you.” 📜
“What [would|do|are] you like?” — “[I’d like|I like|I’m like] a tea and a croissant.” 🥐
“Have you got [any|some|a] biscuits?” — “Yes, we’ve got [some|any|a] today.” 🍪
“Sorry, we haven’t got [any|some|no] milk.” — “No problem. Just [a|some|any] sandwich, then.” 🥪

acts.title: At the counter
text: “Can I take your order?” — “A burger and chips, please.” 🍔🍟
Later: “Is everything OK here?” — “Fine, thank you.”
“Would you like anything else?” — “No, thanks. Can we have the bill, please?” 🧾

o: Can I see the menu, please?

items.sit: You are the waiter. You offer the customer a dessert.
items.why: Would you like…? offers. Do you like…? asks about taste in general.

A sandwich and a water, please.

write.q: Write your café order: 5 lines. Ask for the menu, order a drink and food, ask a question with any, and ask for the bill.
write.model: Can I see the menu, please? I’d like a coffee and a croissant. Have you got any biscuits? And some water, please. Can we have the bill, please?

speak.q: Say your café order out loud. Then be the waiter and offer a dessert.
speak.model: I’d like a tea and a sandwich, please. Have you got any chips? — Would you like a dessert?
